page: Amazon Web Services hpc6a.48xlarge is a high performance computing instance based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 96 dedicated physical cores across an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with a 3.6 GHz clock speed, operating without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory is configured with 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier parallel compute capability, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score of 286,781.38, a PassMark CPU score of 105,393.73, and Geekbench software compilation at 63,259.0. Memory throughput reaches 263.45 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 129.27 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached block reads achieve 12,154.54 GB/sec. Parallel throughput is further evidenced by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1,042.91 GB/sec and Redis SET operations exceeding 179 million operations per second.

Single-core performance is moderate, reflecting the architecture's focus on aggregate compute density rather than extreme single-thread clock frequencies. Benchmarks place single-core stress-ng at 2,988.67 and single-threaded gzip compression at 28.42 GB/sec. Furthermore, the absence of hardware accelerators restricts generative machine learning capabilities; text generation on a 7B LLM executes at 7.95 tokens per second. Relying on remote storage requires accounting for external EBS latency, though the 100 Gbps network provides ample transfer headroom.

Qualitatively, the dedicated physical core architecture and 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio make hpc6a.48xlarge a cost-efficient platform for computational clusters requiring high core density without hyperthreading overhead. It is best suited for compute-bound engineering simulations, Clang builds, parallel scientific workloads, and distributed batch processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc6a.48xlarge is a dedicated high performance computing instance powered by 96 physical AMD EPYC 7R13 cores clocked at 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. With one thread per core and no hyperthreading, the instance pairs its 96 vCPUs with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory and 100 Gbps baseline networking, omitting bundled local storage and GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core computing metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 105,393.73, strong Clang compilation marks, and 179.29 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks and CPU-based LLM generation are modest, the platform delivers high multi-core throughput and high cached memory speeds. It is well suited for compute-intensive batch jobs, CFD simulations, parallel software compilation, and cluster-based scientific workflows.
